input.standard: ASTM E741 (concentration decay, single zone); ASTM D6245 (occupant CO2 as tracer)
input.purpose: Measure the volume of air V_lab served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-v2 as V = Qe * tau, from a reduced-speed rise then a full-speed decay with the two Lab occupants as the CO2 source.

steps.why: Rise: reduced speed (the floor) lowers Qe to 0.3 m3/min so CO2 climbs towards a higher equilibrium; hatch closed and held.
Decay: full speed (Qe about 1 m3/min), record decay towards equilibrium; about one time constant or more; hatch unchanged.

abort.when: the device refuses a step's command
a monitored person out of the 45-120 bpm band, monitoring lost, or one more person in the Lab

monitoring.reason: The two Lab occupants breathe the air whose CO2 the test raises; the hab-b crew are behind the closed hatch.

occupancy.at: before the test, held during it

expected.start: CO2 about 2000 ppm at the start (measured), 1000 ppm under the 3000 ppm limit and above the 200 ppm headroom.
expected.rise: At 30 percent, Qe about 0.3 m3/min. With 2 occupants at 0.38 L/min awake (0.76 L/min) and V about 30 m3 (first guess, stated as such), the initial slope is about +5 ppm/min, so about +90 to +100 ppm over 20 min (about 2100 ppm), well under 3000 ppm. Tau at 30 percent about 100 min, so the rise is only a fraction of a time constant; it is a compromise with the 60 min bound.
expected.decay: At full speed, Qe about 1 m3/min, tau = V/Qe about 30 min (plus a scrubber lag of 3.33 min); the equilibrium is about G/Qe = 0.76 L/min / 1 m3/min = about 760 ppm above supply air. Over 35 min the CO2 should fall about two thirds of the way to it. Fit C(t) = C_eq + (C0 - C_eq) exp(-t/tau) and give V_lab = Qe * tau, expected 10 to 200 m3, about 30 m3.
expected.refutation: The one-zone, closed-hatch hypothesis is refuted if Hab-B CO2 moves with the Lab during the test, if the fit residuals are systematic, if C_eq from the fit differs strongly from G/Qe, or if the Lab CO2 does not rise at 30 percent. The rise phase would be unusable if the rise stays within sensor noise, and then only the decay gives tau.
expected.stop: The test stops at once on any abort condition; CO2 must stay under 3000 ppm and abort at 3200 ppm.

hypotheses: The Lab is one well-mixed zone; the Lab-Hab-B hatch is held closed in both steps and the exchange through the closed hatch (design ventilation 3 m3/min per station-topology) is not measured here: it is a hypothesis, not assumed zero. Hab-B CO2 is recorded to show whether the opening exchanges air.
Occupants stay at 2 in the Lab at a steady awake activity of 0.38 L/min each (band 0.26 to 0.45); a person entering or leaving invalidates the curve.
Qe at full speed is the datasheet 1 m3/min (0.3 single-pass efficiency x 3.3 m3/min) and scales linearly with speed; a first guess of V of 30 m3 gives tau of about 30 min.
The rise phase at the 30 percent floor is much shorter than its own time constant (about 100 min); the volume comes mainly from the full-speed decay.
The CO2 sensor co2-1-v2 is accurate and its noise is small against the several-hundred ppm decay; the starting 2000 ppm is not an equilibrium at full speed, so C_eq is fitted, not assumed.
Records: Lab CO2 every minute, Hab-B CO2, the scrubber speed commands and whether each was accepted.
